title: Guardrails: retention policy for eval artifacts + minimal audit log fields
author: Felix Schneider
release_notes:
- Guardrails eval artifacts are now retained for a bounded period (configurable) and cleaned up automatically.
- Audit logs for Optimize config changes now store only minimal required gating fields (no raw prompt/eval payloads).
body: Summary: This PR adds a formal retention policy for guardrails eval artifacts (per-run blobs) and DB summaries, and tightens OptimizeConfigChange audit events to keep only the minimal required fields for compliance/auditability. Motivation: We’ve started persisting more gating artifacts (runner outputs, grader traces, attachments). Without explicit retention, storage grows unbounded and audit logs risk carrying unnecessary payload. This also addresses customer requests for auditability without retaining raw eval data (SUP-18544). What’s included: 1) Eval artifact retention (object store): Introduce TTL-based lifecycle for guardrails artifacts in object storage. Default retention: 30 days for standard tiers, 90 days for Enterprise (configurable via GuardrailsRetentionPolicy). Artifacts covered: per-prompt outputs, grader traces, and rendered HTML summaries. We retain a small pointer record (eval_run_id -> artifact prefix) even after artifacts expire. 2) Eval summary retention (DB): Add created_at indexing + a scheduled cleanup job that deletes old GuardrailsEvalRunDetails rows beyond retention window while keeping GuardrailsEvalRunSummary rows for 13 months (aggregated metrics only). The summary record is what the console uses for the ‘gating results’ panel after artifacts are deleted. 3) Minimal audit log fields: Update OptimizeConfigChange audit emission to remove any embedded metric arrays / per-prompt deltas. Audit events now include: tenant_id, actor, config_delta_hash, model_id/model_version, prompt_set_id + prompt_set_revision, suite_id + suite_revision, guardrail_policy_id + policy_version, decision (pass/fail/timeout/override), failure_reason_codes, eval_run_id(s), and timestamps. No raw prompts, no generated outputs, no grader traces, and no full metric distributions. 4) Export/SIEM safety: Add an allowlist-based serializer for audit payloads to ensure future fields don’t accidentally leak large data. Enforce payload size limits at serialization time (hard cap 16KB) with a metric + structured warning when truncation would have occurred. 5) Tests + migration: Includes migration for new retention policy table and backfill defaults for existing tenants. Adds unit tests for retention window computation, cleanup job behavior, and audit payload allowlist. Implementation details: - New table guardrails_retention_policies (tenant_id, tier, artifact_ttl_days, detail_ttl_days, summary_ttl_days, updated_by, updated_at). - New worker GuardrailsRetentionJanitor runs daily (02:00 UTC) and emits metrics: guardrails.retention.deleted_artifacts_count, guardrails.retention.deleted_db_rows_count, guardrails.retention.errors_total. - Object store lifecycle: for hosted we apply bucket lifecycle rules by prefix (guardrails/runs/...) and TTL tags; for private/on-prem we fall back to janitor-driven deletes via the storage abstraction (best-effort, rate-limited). - Audit event schema: OptimizeConfigChange now stores gating_details_ref instead of gating_details; gating_details_ref contains eval_run_id(s) and policy/suite/prompt-set version identifiers. The console fetches the full summary via the guardrails service (RBAC-checked) rather than from audit logs. Notes / decisions: - We intentionally keep GuardrailsEvalRunSummary longer than artifacts to support historical investigations without storing raw model outputs. - Overrides: audit logs keep override_justification and approver fields (already required), but still do not include raw eval artifacts. - Private deployments: retention windows are configurable; default remains 30/90 but can be set to 0 for artifacts to disable persistence entirely (summary-only). Follow-ups: - Separate PR will update docs/runbooks to mention artifact expiration behavior in the console UI (ticket: ENG-3925). - We may want a small ‘download before expiry’ banner in the console once retention is enforced. Testing: - Unit: guardrails/retention/*, audit/allowlist_serializer_test. - Integration: e2e applies still pass; updated snapshot tests for OptimizeConfigChange event shape. Rollout: - Feature-flagged via guardrails.retention_policy.enabled (default on in staging, off in prod until SRE signoff). - Janitor runs in dry-run mode for 48h in prod; then toggled to delete-enabled. Security: Reviewed with Naomi Feldman; audit payload allowlist + caps ensure SIEM exports remain small and PII-safe.
commits: guardrails: add retention policy model + admin plumbing
guardrails: implement retention janitor (db cleanup + artifact deletes)
audit: switch OptimizeConfigChange to minimal gating fields + allowlist serializer
tests: retention windows + audit payload size enforcement
migrations: backfill default retention by tenant tier
review_conversation:
Naomi Feldman: Can we confirm no raw model outputs can end up in audit logs indirectly (e.g., via failure_reason_details)? Also want an explicit payload cap.
Felix Schneider (author): Yep—failure_reason_details removed; only reason codes remain. Added allowlist serializer + hard cap 16KB with metric guardrails.audit_payload_truncated_total.
Naomi Feldman: Approved once the cap is enforced before enqueueing to the audit pipeline.
Felix Schneider (author): Updated—cap enforced in AuditEventEmitter before publish; tests added.

Jordan Lee: Retention windows: why keep summaries 13 months? And is the cleanup job deterministic across regions?
Felix Schneider (author): 13 months aligns with typical enterprise audit cycles + quarterly reviews. Cleanup queries are scoped by tenant + created_at and run per-region worker; emits per-region metrics for drift. Also added an index on (tenant_id, created_at) to keep it bounded.
Jordan Lee: Looks good—please add a comment clarifying that summaries are aggregated and PII-free.
Felix Schneider (author): Added comment + link to audit/PII guidelines in code.

Logan Wright: The new metrics labels—please avoid tenant_id labels on retention metrics.
Felix Schneider (author): Agreed; retention metrics are aggregated by tier + region only. No tenant labels.
Logan Wright: Approved.

Sean Gallagher: For prod rollout, can we run janitor in dry-run first and alert on deletion counts? Also ensure rate limiting on object deletes.
Felix Schneider (author): Added dry-run mode + config flag, plus rate limiter (500 deletes/min/region). Included dashboards hook metric guardrails.retention.planned_deletes_count.
Sean Gallagher: Approved with dry-run default.
merge_outcome: Merged (squash) by Connor O'Brien after approvals; feature flag left OFF in prod pending SRE rollout checklist signoff.
